description: Updates settings tab within the runner Settings panel. Allows users to check for and install application updates. The page auto-checks for updates on mount via the Tauri `check_for_updates` IPC command. It renders a permanent 'current version' card (showing the installed version and last-checked timestamp) and a conditional status card that shows one of four states: checking/idle (no card), development mode (update checking disabled), update available (with release notes and install button), or up to date. A separate error card appears if a check or install fails. An informational tip box is always visible at the bottom.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The Updates tab renders a SectionHeader with a Download icon, title 'Updates', and a description line. Below it are two always-visible structural elements: the current version card and the info tip box. A third conditional card appears after a check completes.

assertions.description: A heading with text 'Updates' is present as the section title
A description paragraph reading 'Check for and install application updates to get the latest features and bug fixes.' is visible below the heading

criteria.textContent: Check for and install application updates to get the latest features and bug fixes.

assertions.description: A tip box is always visible with text 'Tip: Updates are checked automatically when this settings tab is opened. You can also manually check for updates using the button above.'

The page layout has exactly two always-present sections: the current version card (top) and the tip box (bottom). A third conditional status card appears between them only after a check completes. There are no sub-tabs, no nested navigation, and no modal dialogs within this tab.

groups.name: Current Version Card
groups.description: A card that is always visible showing the currently installed application version and when updates were last checked. Also contains the 'Check for Updates' button.

assertions.description: An element with data-content-role='metric' and data-content-label='current version' is present, showing the installed version string (e.g., 'v0.1.0')

An element with data-content-role='body-text' and data-content-label='last checked time' is present. It shows either 'Never' (if no check has run) or a human-readable timestamp of the most recent check.
A 'Check for Updates' button is present in the current version card

The version string displayed in data-content-label='current version' must match the actual application version. It should appear in a 'vX.Y.Z' semver format prefixed with 'v'. The last-checked timestamp updates each time a check completes — on first load it shows 'Never', and after the auto-check on mount it shows the time of that check.

groups.name: Check for Updates Button Interaction
groups.description: The 'Check for Updates' button triggers an update check via the Tauri `check_for_updates` command. During the check the button is disabled and shows a spinner. After the check completes the status card is updated and the last-checked timestamp is refreshed.

assertions.description: The 'Check for Updates' button is enabled when the status is idle (not currently checking or installing)
assertions.precondition: Page is in idle state (no check or install in progress)

assertions.description: The 'Check for Updates' button is disabled while a check is in progress. The button shows a spinning RefreshCw icon alongside the label 'Checking...' to indicate an in-progress operation.
assertions.precondition: A check has been triggered but not yet completed

assertions.description: Clicking 'Check for Updates' invokes the Tauri `check_for_updates` command. While the command is running the button is disabled and shows a spinner icon. After completion: (a) the last-checked timestamp is updated to the current time; (b) the conditional status card appears or refreshes; (c) the button returns to its enabled 'Check for Updates' state. If the command throws an error the error card appears instead of the status card.
assertions.precondition: Page is in idle state

groups.name: Automatic Check on Tab Load
groups.description: The UpdateSettings component automatically triggers a `check_for_updates` call via useEffect when it first mounts. The user does not need to click anything — the check runs immediately and the status card populates once it completes.

assertions.description: When the Updates tab is first opened, the 'Check for Updates' button immediately transitions to the 'Checking...' disabled state without any user interaction, indicating the automatic on-mount check is running.
assertions.precondition: The Updates settings tab has just been opened for the first time in this session

assertions.description: After the automatic on-mount check completes, a status card appears showing one of: development mode notice, update available, or up to date. The last-checked timestamp also transitions from 'Never' to the current time. This entire flow happens without any user interaction.
assertions.precondition: The Updates settings tab has just been opened

groups.name: Development Mode Status Card
groups.description: In debug/development builds the `check_for_updates` command returns `{ available: false, development: true }`. The component renders a 'Development Mode' status card with an informational message explaining that update checking is disabled in development builds.

assertions.description: An element with data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='development mode' is visible showing the text 'Development Mode'
assertions.precondition: Running a debug/development build and a check has completed

assertions.description: The development mode card displays the message 'Update checking is disabled in development builds. Build a release version to enable automatic updates.'

criteria.textContent: Update checking is disabled in development builds.

assertions.precondition: Development mode status card is shown

assertions.description: The development mode card does NOT show a 'Download and Install Update' button. No install action is available in development mode because `install_update` also returns a dev-mode error in debug builds.
assertions.precondition: Development mode status card is shown

groups.name: Update Available Status Card
groups.description: When `check_for_updates` returns `{ available: true, version, current_version, notes }`, the component renders an 'Update Available' card showing the new version, optional release notes, and a 'Download and Install Update' button.

assertions.description: An element with data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='update available' is visible showing 'Update Available' when a newer version exists
assertions.precondition: check_for_updates returned available=true

assertions.description: The update available card displays a description saying 'Version {version} is available for download' where {version} is the version string from the API response (e.g., 'Version 1.2.3 is available for download')
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown

assertions.description: When the API response includes release notes (non-empty `notes` field), the update available card shows a 'Release Notes' section label and a scrollable container (max-h-48) displaying the notes text
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown and the API response included non-empty notes

assertions.description: A full-width 'Download and Install Update' button is present in the update available card
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown

assertions.description: A note reading 'The application will restart automatically after the update is installed.' is visible below the install button

criteria.textContent: The application will restart automatically after the update is installed.

assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown

groups.name: Install Update Flow
groups.description: Clicking 'Download and Install Update' invokes the Tauri `install_update` command, which downloads the update package and restarts the application. During install, the button is disabled and shows an 'Installing Update...' label with a spinner.

assertions.description: The 'Download and Install Update' button is enabled when the update available card is shown and no install is in progress
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown and status is not 'installing'

assertions.description: While install_update is running, the install button shows 'Installing Update...' with a spinner icon and is disabled. The 'Check for Updates' button in the version card is also disabled during this time.
assertions.precondition: User has clicked 'Download and Install Update' and the command is in progress

assertions.description: On a successful install_update response the application restarts automatically — the Rust handler calls `updater.download_and_install()` then `app_handle.restart()`. There is no post-install UI state in this component; the window closes/reopens as part of the restart. An error card is shown only if the command returns an error (e.g., in dev mode or if the download fails).
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown and user clicks the install button

groups.name: Up to Date Status Card
groups.description: When `check_for_updates` returns `{ available: false }` without the development flag, the component renders an 'Up to Date' card with a green CheckCircle icon confirming the user is on the latest version.

assertions.description: An element with data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='up to date' is visible showing 'Up to Date' when no update is available
assertions.precondition: check_for_updates returned available=false without development=true

assertions.description: The up-to-date card displays the message "You're running the latest version of Qontinui Runner."

criteria.textContent: You're running the latest version of Qontinui Runner.

assertions.precondition: Up to date card is shown

assertions.description: When the 'Up to Date' card is shown, the 'Download and Install Update' button is not present anywhere on the page — there is nothing to install
assertions.precondition: Up to date card is shown

groups.name: Error State
groups.description: If `check_for_updates` or `install_update` throws an exception, the component stores the error message in state and renders an error card with an AlertCircle icon and the error text. The status card is not shown when an error card is displayed.

assertions.description: An element with data-content-role='status' and data-content-label='update error' is visible showing 'Update Error' when a check or install fails
assertions.precondition: check_for_updates or install_update threw an error

assertions.description: The error card displays the actual error message string returned by the failed command (e.g., network error, permission error). The message is rendered as-is from the JavaScript Error.message value.
assertions.precondition: Error card is shown

assertions.description: After an error occurs, the 'Check for Updates' button returns to its enabled state so the user can retry. The error card persists until the next check is triggered.
assertions.precondition: An error card is displayed after a failed check

groups.name: Status Card Mutual Exclusion
groups.description: Only one status card variant can be shown at a time. The four possible status card states (development mode, update available, up to date, and nothing) are mutually exclusive — they are driven by a single `updateInfo` nullable value and a single `error` nullable string. The error card and status card are also mutually exclusive.

assertions.description: At most one of the following status labels is visible at any time: 'development mode', 'update available', 'up to date', 'update error'. The status cards for these states are rendered by separate conditional branches in the component — they cannot coexist. If two status labels are visible simultaneously, there is a rendering bug.
assertions.precondition: A check has completed

assertions.description: While a check is in progress (status='checking'), no status card is visible — the previous result is cleared when a new check starts. Only the current version card and tip box are shown during the checking phase.
assertions.precondition: A check has been triggered and is in progress

groups.name: IPC Response Data Model
groups.description: The page relies on two Tauri IPC commands. Their response shapes determine which UI state is shown. Both commands behave differently in debug vs release builds, which is critical for verifying behavior in the correct build context.

assertions.description: The `check_for_updates` command returns a CommandResponse where `data` is an UpdateInfo object: `{ available: boolean, version?: string, current_version?: string, notes?: string, development?: boolean }`. In release builds: `available=true` when a newer version exists on the update server, `available=false` when current. In debug builds: `available=false, development=true` always. The UI must correctly branch on `available` and `development` flags to choose the status card variant.

The `install_update` command returns `{ success: true, message: 'Update installed. The application will restart.', data: { installed: true, version: string } }` on success. In debug builds it returns `{ success: false, message: 'Updates are disabled in development mode', data: { installed: false, development: true } }`. A `success: false` response from a release build should be treated as an error (shown via the error card), not as a dev-mode notice.
assertions.precondition: Update available card is shown

states.name: Checking for Updates
states.description: An update check is in progress. The 'Check for Updates' button shows 'Checking...' and is disabled. No status card is visible.

transitions.name: Check completed — development mode
transitions.description: Check returned development=true; dev mode card appears

transitions.name: Check completed — update available
transitions.description: Check returned available=true; update available card appears

transitions.name: Check completed — up to date
transitions.description: Check returned available=false without development flag; up to date card appears

transitions.name: Check failed
transitions.description: Check threw an exception; error card appears

states.name: Development Mode
states.description: Update check returned development=true. Dev mode card is visible. Check button is re-enabled.

states.name: Update Available
states.description: An update is available. The update available card is shown with version info, optional release notes, and the install button.

transitions.name: Recheck for updates
transitions.description: User clicks 'Check for Updates' to recheck

states.name: Up to Date
states.description: No update available. The up to date card is shown with a green CheckCircle icon.

transitions.name: Recheck for updates
transitions.description: User clicks 'Check for Updates' to run a fresh check

states.name: Installing Update
states.description: install_update command is running. The install button shows 'Installing Update...' and is disabled. The app will restart automatically on success.

transitions.name: Install failed
transitions.description: install_update returned an error (e.g., dev mode, download failure)

states.name: Error
states.description: A check or install command threw an error. The error card is shown with the error message. The 'Check for Updates' button is re-enabled to allow retrying.

transitions.name: Retry check
transitions.description: User clicks 'Check for Updates' to retry
